Artist.value: El Greco

ImageDescription.value: The Burial of the Lord of Orgaz (El entierro del señor de Orgaz), better known as The Burial of the Count of Orgaz (El entierro del conde de Orgaz) is an oil painting on canvas in the Mannerist style by El Greco, painted between 1586 and 1588. It was commissioned for the Church of Santo Tomé in Toledo, Spain, where it remains today, and is considered one of the painter's greatest masterpieces. The painting depicts the miracle in which, according to tradition, Saint Stephen and Saint Augustine of Hippo descended from heaven to personally bury Gonzalo Ruiz de Toledo, lord of the town of Orgaz, who died in 1323 (or, according to other sources, in 1312), in the Church of Santo Tomé, as a reward for his exemplary life of devotion, humility, and charitable works. El Greco accepted the commission to paint the work in 1586, more than two and a half centuries after the events it depicts.

ImageDescription.value: Jean de Dinteville, French Ambassador to the court of Henry VIII of England, and Georges de Selve, Bishop of Lavaur. The painting is famous for containing, in the foreground, at the bottom, a spectacular anamorphic, which, from an oblique point of view, is revealed to be a human skull. An Armenian carpet, a vishapagorg rug from Central Anatolia, is on the table.
